title: Realize a finite tower of elementary etale local bases by one pointed neighbourhood
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $s\in S$, and $A_0=\mathcal O_{S,s}$. Fix an integer $d\geq0$. For $1\leq j\leq d$, let $U_j\to\operatorname{Spec}A_{j-1}$ be an affine etale morphism of finite presentation, let $u_j\in U_j$ lie over the closed point and induce an isomorphism of residue fields, and put $A_j=\mathcal O_{U_j,u_j}$. Here etale means [def-weil-etale-morphism], finite presentation means [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] together with quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness, and local rings and residue fields are [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-residue-field]. There exist a scheme $S'$, a point $s'\in S'$, and an etale morphism $e:S'\to S$ with $e(s')=s$ and $\kappa(s)\cong\kappa(s')$, together with an isomorphism $A_d\cong\mathcal O_{S',s'}$ of $\mathcal O_{S,s}$-algebras whose structural map is the composite of the given local-ring maps. The induced residue-field isomorphism agrees with their composite. When $d=0$ one may take $(S',s')=(S,s)$. For every morphism $f:X\to S$ and $x\in X$ with $f(x)=s$, the fibre of $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A_d\to X$ over $x$ is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$, and its unique point maps to the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A_d$. Equivalently the canonical maps identify $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}A_d$ with $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(s')\cong\kappa(x)$. Spectra and fibre products are [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product]; tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

proof.text: Induct on $j\in\{0,\ldots,d\}$ with invariant: there is a pointed scheme $(T_j,t_j)$ etale over $(S,s)$ and an isomorphism $\theta_j:\mathcal O_{T_j,t_j}\cong A_j$ whose map from $A_0$ is precisely the first $j$ given local maps. Its residue map is their composite. For $j=0$, take $(T_0,t_0)=(S,s)$ and the identity. The identity is an open immersion and hence etale by (1) of the cited permanence lemma.

source.place: Tag 05I5, proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point, first proof, first paragraph: finitely many elementary etale replacements

proof.text: Assume the invariant at $j<d$. Choose an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset T_j$ containing $t_j$, with corresponding prime $p$. The affine-open stalk lemma identifies $R_p$ with $\mathcal O_{T_j,t_j}$ compatibly with germs. Through $\theta_j$ regard $U_{j+1}=\operatorname{Spec}B$ as etale over $\operatorname{Spec}R_p$; write $r\subset B$ for $u_{j+1}$. The unpointed etale model lemma gives an etale $R$-algebra $C$, a map $i:C\to B$, and a multiplicative subset $M\subset C$ such that $B=M^{-1}C$, with $R\to C\to B$ exactly $R\to R_p\cong A_j\to B$. This applies to the given affine etale morphism, with no Noetherian hypothesis.

Put $q=i^{-1}(r)$. It is prime, avoids $M$ because elements of $M$ become units in $B$, and contracts to $p$ in $R$ because the given point lies over the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}R_p$. There is a canonical isomorphism $C_q\cong B_r$: send $c/t$ to $i(c)/i(t)$. Conversely $C\to C_q$ inverts $M$, so it extends to $B=M^{-1}C\to C_q$ by $i(c)/i(m)\mapsto c/m$. For $b=i(c)/i(m)\notin r$, necessarily $c\notin q$, so its image $c/m$ is a unit; thus this extends to $B_r\to C_q$. Both composites fix every numerator from $C$ and every inverted denominator, so are identities by the fraction definition. The maps preserve the specified structural map from $R_p$, not merely the abstract local rings. This is the elementary fraction argument for the localization supplied in the preceding step.

Take $T_{j+1}=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $t_{j+1}=q$, and use $T_{j+1}\to W\hookrightarrow T_j\to S$. The first arrow is etale by the model, the middle is an open immersion, and etale maps compose. The affine stalk and Spec-map stalk lemmas identify its local map with the fraction map $R_p\to C_q$. Composing $C_q\cong B_r=\mathcal O_{U_{j+1},u_{j+1}}=A_{j+1}$ with these identifications proves the invariant. Passing to the quotients by maximal ideals gives exactly the given residue-field map, an isomorphism by hypothesis. Hence $\theta_{j+1}$ and its residue map compose with the preceding ones as required. Induction ends with $(S^{\prime},s^{\prime})=(T_d,t_d)$; invert $\theta_d$ for the isomorphism in the statement. At $d=0$ retain $S$ itself.

proof.text: For each $1\le j\le d$, let $\mathfrak m_{j-1}$ be the maximal ideal of $A_{j-1}$, write $U_j=\operatorname{Spec}B_j$, and let $r_j$ be its marked prime. Base change and the etale-over-field lemma give $B_j/\mathfrak m_{j-1}B_j\cong\prod_{a=1}^n L_a$ with each $L_a/\kappa(A_{j-1})$ finite separable. The quotient-localization lemma identifies $A_j/\mathfrak m_{j-1}A_j$ with the localization of that product at the prime induced by $r_j$ (which contains $\mathfrak m_{j-1}B_j$). This is one field factor: the prime is the kernel of one projection by the finite-product spectrum lemma; the idempotent of that factor is outside the prime, and inverting it kills all other factors. Thus the quotient is a field, so $\mathfrak m_{j-1}A_j=\mathfrak m_j$. Its structural map from $\kappa(A_{j-1})$ is the given residue-field isomorphism, not an arbitrary field isomorphism. In particular the nonempty marked fibre ensures $n\ge1$.

proof.text: Extension of ideals is associative: the ideal generated in $A_j$ by $\mathfrak m_0$ equals the extension of the ideal it generates in $A_{j-1}$, since both consist of finite sums of images of elements of $\mathfrak m_0$ times elements of $A_j$. Induction using the previous step gives $\mathfrak m_0 A_d=\mathfrak m_d$ and identifies $A_d/\mathfrak m_0A_d=\kappa(A_d)$ with $\kappa(s)$ via the composite residue map. Consequently for any field $K$ over $\kappa(s)$ the map $K\otimes_{A_0}A_d\to K$, $b\otimes a\mapsto b\,\overline a$, is an isomorphism, inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Here $\overline a\in\kappa(s)$ is defined by the inverse composite residue isomorphism. To check the inverse on $b\otimes a$, lift $\overline a$ to $a_0\in A_0$; then $a-a_0\in\mathfrak m_0 A_d$ vanishes in the tensor product and balancing gives $b\otimes a=b\overline a\otimes1$. This also proves canonically $K\otimes_{A_0}A_d\cong K\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(s^{\prime})$ using step 4.

source.place: Tag 05I5, proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point, unique-point clause; explicit residue-field calculation

proof.text: For $f:X\to S$ and $x$ over $s$, put $K=\kappa(x)$ with its induced $\kappa(s)$-algebra structure. By the fibre-product universal property (pasting of the two cartesian squares) the fibre over $x$ is $\operatorname{Spec}K\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A_d$, where $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ is $f\circ j_x$ with $j_x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ the canonical residue-field morphism. By residue-field naturality $f\circ j_x=j_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(s)\to K)$, and $j_s$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the residue map $A_0\to\kappa(s)$ followed by the canonical $g_s:\operatorname{Spec}A_0\to S$; the second map is $g_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(A_0\to A_d)$. Choose an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\ni s$ with prime $p$ and open immersion $\iota_W$. By the affine-open stalk lemma $R_p\cong A_0$ compatibly with germs, and $\iota_W\circ\operatorname{Spec}(R\to R_p)$ and $g_s$ both send the closed point to $s$ with the identity stalk map $A_0\to A_0$, so they are equal by the classification of morphisms from the spectrum of a local ring. Thus both maps factor through $\iota_W$, and since $\iota_W$ is a monomorphism a cone over $S$ of the two factored maps is the same as a cone over $\operatorname{Spec}R$: the fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}K\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}A_d$. The affine fibre-product lemma identifies it with $\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_RA_d)$ compatibly with both projections, and $K\otimes_RA_d=K\otimes_{A_0}A_d$ because the elements of $R\setminus p$ already act invertibly on both factors. By step 6 this is $\operatorname{Spec}K$. The map $A_d\to K$ is the residue map followed by the field embedding $\kappa(s)\to K$, so its kernel is exactly $\mathfrak m_d$. Its unique point consequently maps to the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A_d$.

The delivery is a first split: there is no repair note, the item is still unsplit in both clones, there are no new nodes and the statement is unchanged. The statement is true; I tested d=0, d=1 over a field with a split factor, a non-reduced base and a non-trivial residue extension (excluded by the hypothesis). It is not a duplicate: the etale-triples-prime-localization family is pointed over a separable-closure K. Steps 1-6 are correct. Step 2: the model node gives C, a, i and M with a then i equal to R to R_p to B and B a localization of C at M. Step 3: the fraction argument C_q = B_r is elementary. Step 4: the stalk map follows from the affine-open stalk lemma and the Spec-map stalk lemma. Step 5: etale base change plus the field-product lemma, with the quotient-localization lemma applied to I = m_{j-1}B_j inside r_j, gives m_{j-1}A_j = m_j. Step 6: an explicit balanced-tensor inverse. C1 fault in step 7, repaired: three facts it used had no node. These are (a) f composed with j_x factors through Spec kappa(s), lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality; (b) Spec O_{S,s} to S factors through the affine chart, lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring with the affine-open stalk lemma; (c) the fibre product over S becomes one over Spec R because an open immersion is a monomorphism, lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism. The fix rewrites step 7 and adds these to its uses and to proof_deps; all three are Mathlib leaves and no cycle arises.
